info.title: Memoria API
info.description: Search API over your own accumulated record: agent transcripts, issues, pull requests and notes, served from a QMD index behind one authenticated front door. Retrieval is QMD's hybrid BM25 plus vector search with LLM reranking; Memoria adds network exposure, collection scoping and client tooling.

servers.description: The origin this document was fetched from.

get.description: The API process is up. Anonymous. Does not contact the search backend; use `/ready` for that.

Probes the memoria-qmd sidecar. Callers without an admin key share one probe per `Memoria:Sidecar:ReadinessCacheTime` (2 s by default): callers in that time share one answer. A caller with an admin key probes on its own, so the sidecar logs the call under that request's trace id. 200 whenever it answers, with `status` of `ready`, `warming` or `degraded`: losing GPU workers makes search rank worse, and must not take the API out of rotation. 503 only when the sidecar cannot be reached, unless `strict=true`, which also answers 503 for anything but `ready`. Anonymous for orchestrators: without an admin key the body carries only the status word, and `not_ready` for an unreachable sidecar, with `reason` and `sidecar` null. An admin key gets the full report, including stuck jobs and documents set aside.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: Answer 503 unless the sidecar is fully ready, with no degradation.

get.description: Hybrid search over the indexed documents: BM25 and vector retrieval fused by reciprocal rank, then reranked by a cross-encoder unless `rerank=false`. Reranked queries take a few seconds; `rerank=false` returns fused results in well under a second. Frontmatter filters (`project`, `branch`, `since`, `until`, `tag`) are applied after retrieval, so a filtered result set can be shorter than `limit` even when more matches exist. `degraded` means the search ran without something a full search uses, such as the reranker: results are valid but may rank worse, and `degradedReasons` says what. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Plain-text query. It is searched as itself, lexically and by vector, unless `expand` asks QMD to expand it.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Let QMD's model expand the query into more lexical and semantic sub-queries first. Slower, and no better on the measured corpus. The server's default is usually false.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Collection to search. Repeat for several; names are case-sensitive. Omitted, a collection-scoped key searches all its collections; other callers get the configured default set, else QMD's default-included collections. A collection outside the key's scope is refused with 403.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum results, 1 to the configured ceiling (100). Default 10.

parameters.name: minScore
parameters.description: Drop results scoring below this, 0 to 1.

parameters.name: rerank
parameters.description: Run the LLM reranker. Default true (full hybrid). false returns sub-second lexical plus vector fusion.

parameters.name: intent
parameters.description: Background context that steers reranking and snippet selection. Does not search on its own.

parameters.name: candidateLimit
parameters.description: Candidates handed to the reranker, 1 to 1000. QMD's default is 40.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Frontmatter filter: `project` equals any of these (case-insensitive). Repeatable.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Frontmatter filter: `git_branch` equals any of these (case-insensitive). Repeatable.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Frontmatter filter: inclusive lower bound on the document's start time, `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO timestamp.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Frontmatter filter: inclusive upper bound; a bare date covers the whole day.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Frontmatter filter: every listed tag must be present (case-insensitive). Repeatable.

get.description: Fetch a document by display path (`collection/path.md`), by `qmd://` URI, or by its six-character docid. `fromLine` and `maxLines` narrow the body to the lines around a search hit; `body=false` returns metadata only. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document reference: `collection/path.md`, `qmd://collection/path.md`, or a docid.

parameters.name: fromLine
parameters.description: First line of the body to return (1-indexed).

parameters.name: maxLines
parameters.description: Number of lines to return from `fromLine`.

parameters.name: lineNumbers
parameters.description: Prefix each body line with `N: `.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: false returns metadata only.

post.description: Batch fetch by a list of references (paths or docids), by a glob such as `claude-sessions/2026-05*.md`, or both. A glob may use only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`; braces, brackets and extglobs are refused with 400. Bodies are capped at `maxBytes` each (default 64 KiB, at most 1 MiB); documents over the cap are listed under `skipped`. For a collection-scoped key every list is filtered per result and `errors` is always empty: a reference that matched nothing the key may read is simply absent. Requires the `read` scope.

get.description: Every collection the caller may search, with its active document count and root context. Requires the `read` scope.

Totals for the collections the caller may read, whether a vector index exists, and per-collection counts. `needsEmbedding` is the backlog for the whole index, so it is null for a collection-scoped key. `unredactedCollections` lists what an operator stored unredacted. Only a key with the `admin` scope as well sees it; it is null for anyone else. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Creates a key and returns its plaintext. This response is the only time the plaintext exists. `read` and `ingest` keys must list `collections` or set `allCollections` to true; an empty list is refused. A key with only the `admin` scope omits both. Scopes do not imply each other: `admin` does not grant `read`. With `Memoria:Auth:DefaultKeyLifetime` set, a key without the `admin` scope and with no `expiresAt` expires that long after it is made. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Every key, including revoked and expired ones. Never includes key material. Requires the `admin` scope.

delete.description: Takes effect on the key's next request. Revoking a revoked key succeeds and keeps the original timestamp. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Replaces the key's secret and returns the new plaintext, once. The id, scopes, collections and expiry stay; the previous token stops working immediately. A revoked or expired key cannot be rotated (409). Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Each worker's state, circuits, load and error rate, and whether it is drained. Empty in local LLM mode. Never includes tokens. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Takes the worker out of rotation. Calls in flight finish and it gets no new ones; `inFlight` shows them leave. Held in the sidecar's memory, so a sidecar restart puts it back. Draining a drained worker changes nothing. Requires the `admin` scope.
Returns the worker to rotation. Enabling a worker that is not drained changes nothing. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Jobs by state, whether the queue is paused, whether jobs persist, documents set aside, model calls by priority class, and the jobs the sidecar remembers, newest first. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Starts no more reindex or embedding jobs. A running job runs to its end; cancel it to stop it sooner. Writes still land and queue, so until the queue resumes new documents are not searchable and deleted ones still are. Held in the sidecar's memory, so a sidecar restart resumes. Requires the `admin` scope.
Lets waiting jobs start again. Requires the `admin` scope.
Queues a failed job again under the same id. 409 unless it has failed. Requires the `admin` scope.

Stops a job that has not finished. A waiting job ends at once; a running one stops at its next safe point, so it may still read `running` here. A cancelled job reports `failed` with the error `Cancelled`. 409 if it has already finished. Requires the `admin` scope.

Rescans the collections' directories and, unless `embed` is false, embeds what changed. Omit `collections` for every collection; an empty list is refused. `force` re-embeds every document, which is expensive. Jobs run one at a time, and an identical job already waiting is returned instead of a new one. Requires the `admin` scope.

Renders the envelope to frontmatter, redacts the whole document, and stores it. No caller can turn redaction off: only an operator can, for a named collection, and `redaction` in the response says which applied. A document redaction cannot finish is refused with 422. `source` and `sourceId` are its identity: sending them again overwrites, and `updated` orders versions, so an older version gets 409. The response counts what was replaced, by rule, with no values. The document becomes searchable when the job finishes. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: restoreDeleted
parameters.description: Stores this even though it was deleted, including the same content. Needs a key with the `admin` scope as well.

delete.description: Names a document by `source` and `sourceId`, or by `path` within the collection, and removes it, waiting for any write of it in progress to finish first. 503 `delete_unconfirmed` means it could not be confirmed done, and repeating it is safe. A deleted document stays searchable until the index changes, so an update starts at once, or within `reindexInSeconds` when one just ran in this collection: `reindexState` says which. It also stops an older copy, or the same content under a later date, being stored again. Safe to repeat: a missing document answers `deleted: false` and costs no update. When `reindexState` is `failed`, repeat the request. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: The collection the document is in.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source it was stored under. Use with `sourceId`.

parameters.name: sourceId
parameters.description: Its identity within that source.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Its path within the collection, instead of `source` and `sourceId`.

post.description: The body is the raw JSONL of a Claude Code or Codex session, read as a stream. It is rendered and redacted here into one or more parts. 202 means every part arrived. 207 means not all of it is stored: `parts` and `read` say why, the session stays `partial`, and when `retryable` is true sending the same upload again finishes it. A transcript with no messages, or that lost any, is never 202. An older version than the one stored gets 409, as does a second upload of the session while one is running, a file the ledger does not say is this session's, and messages that do not start with the stored ones, unless `allowShrink` is set. Parts it no longer has are deleted last, and a part someone deleted stays deleted. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: The collection to write to.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `claude` or `codex`.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session's id, normally the transcript's file name without its extension.

parameters.name: projectDirectory
parameters.description: The Claude Code project folder the transcript was in. Tells apart two copies of one session.

parameters.name: allowShrink
parameters.description: Set when the session's history really did change. Without it, an upload whose messages do not start with the stored ones is refused, as it looks just like a cut or damaged copy.

parameters.name: restoreDeleted
parameters.description: Writes parts of this session that were deleted, which otherwise stay deleted. Needs a key with the `admin` scope as well.

parameters.name: updated
parameters.description: When this copy of the transcript last changed, as an ISO timestamp. Orders uploads, so an older one is refused.

get.description: Only `complete` means all of it arrived. `partial` means some parts may be searchable, and the upload should be sent again. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: The collection to write to.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `claude` or `codex`.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session's id, normally the transcript's file name without its extension.

parameters.name: projectDirectory
parameters.description: The Claude Code project folder the transcript was in. Tells apart two copies of one session.

parameters.name: allowShrink
parameters.description: Set when the session's history really did change. Without it, an upload whose messages do not start with the stored ones is refused, as it looks just like a cut or damaged copy.

parameters.name: restoreDeleted
parameters.description: Writes parts of this session that were deleted, which otherwise stay deleted. Needs a key with the `admin` scope as well.

post.description: For moving an old corpus. The body is the markdown as it is, frontmatter included, and it is stored at `path` as it came, except that all of it goes through the collection's redaction decision. `frontmatter` in the answer says whether the sidecar could read the frontmatter: anything but `read` means the document is searchable but matches no date, project or tag filter. Safe to send again: the path is the identity, an equal `updated` overwrites with the same result, and an older one gets 409. Past the size limit it gets 413, and past the limit on large documents at once it gets 503 with `Retry-After`, so pause before sending again. It cannot delete. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: The collection to write to, which must be open to ingest.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Where it goes, relative to the collection. Its existing path, which identifies it.

parameters.name: updated
parameters.description: When this copy last changed, as an ISO timestamp. Orders versions, so send the same value when sending it again.

get.summary: What is recorded for a rendered document's path
get.description: Says what the ledger holds for a path, so a migration can check what arrived. `none` means nothing is recorded. `complete` means a write of it landed. Requires the `ingest` scope.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: The collection it is in.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Its path within the collection.
